chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The women wear silk and brocade, except in the state of Ihram.
ai.seo_question: Are women allowed to wear silk and brocade in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the general permissibility (jawaaz) of women wearing silk and brocade (dibaj) in daily life, contrasting with the stricter prohibition often applied to men. It specifically carves out an exception for the state of Ihram during Hajj or Umrah, where the luxury of silk is temporarily forbidden for both genders to emphasize humility and equality before God. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly view that the prohibition of silk is not absolute but context-dependent, particularly regarding gender and ritual state.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from one of our companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The women can wear the silk and the brocade except in the Ihraam (for Hajj)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Bukayr from certain persons of our people who have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Women can wear silk garments decorated with embroideries, except in the state of Ihram.’”
